request.topic: How TubeForge keeps captions in sync with a portrait Short
request.angle: Explain the word-to-WAV alignment, highlighted current word, portrait safe-area checks, and three-second pacing gates as TubeForge implementation details. Do not present them as universal YouTube rules.

sources.title: TubeForge README: YouTube Shorts workflow
sources.excerpt: Shorts previews are rendered at 540×960. Approved finals are rendered at 1080×1920, 30 fps with H.264 video and AAC audio. A local waveform aligner binds every approved narration word to its generated WAV before captions are rendered. The final quality gate verifies that alignment against the assembled audio, rejects a first word after three seconds, rejects visual holds over three seconds, and validates portrait caption margins and line widths. Shorts use large uppercase ASS captions near the lower-middle safe area. The currently spoken word is yellow and surrounding words remain white. Scene holds are deterministically divided into shorter camera moves, so a long narration scene does not become one static shot.
